reason: The light-sensitive cells need relay cells to pass their signals onward.
expectation: They should form a retina that detects light and relays signals.

effect: The retinas combine light-sensitive cells with relay cells, so they are ready to be incorporated into the eyes.
reaction: The link from light detection to nerve fibres is clear.
reason: The eye walls provide a structure to hold the retinas.
expectation: The retinas should line the inside of the eye walls.

effect: The retinas now line eye cups with three named slots for the front fittings.
reaction: The marked slots make the next construction steps clear.
reason: The corneas are transparent curved fronts, matching the clear-front slot.
expectation: The corneas should fit into the clear-front slot.

effect: The corneas fill the clear-front slot; the lenses and irises remain to be fitted.
reason: The lenses match the focusing-lenses slot.
expectation: The lenses should fit into the eye cups.

effect: The lenses are fitted, leaving the light-control slot for the irises.
reason: The irises surround the pupils and match the remaining light-control slot.
expectation: The irises should fit into the eye cups.

effect: The eye cups now have all three front fittings, which focus light and control how much enters.
reaction: The explanation makes the fittings' roles clear.
reason: The visual pathways should connect signals from the completed eyes toward the brain.
expectation: The visual pathways should connect to the retinal nerve fibers.

effect: The eyes now have pathways carrying retinal signals toward the brain; eye-moving muscles and the body still need connecting.
reaction: The contrast between incoming light and outgoing nerve signals is helpful.
reason: The eye-moving muscles and nerves should give the connected eyes the movement required by the goal.
expectation: The muscles and nerves should attach to the eyes so they can move.

effect: The eyes are connected to the body and its brain; the eye-moving muscles and nerves still need to be added.
reaction: I was surprised the muscles could not be fitted before connecting the eyes to the body.
reason: The remaining muscles and nerves should give the connected eyes movement.
expectation: The muscles and nerves should connect to the eyes, completing the moving-eye assembly.

effect: The eye muscles and nerves completed the connection, producing a body that can aim its eyes and use retinal signals.
reaction: Seeing the assembled eyes directed toward a face brought the construction together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the visual pathways was most worthwhile: the result clearly distinguished light entering the eye from nerve signals leaving it.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the three front parts was straightforward, but the successive slotting results felt a little repetitive. The explanation after the final fitting helped clarify their roles.

surprise.text: I expected to attach the eye muscles before connecting the eyes to the body, but the compatibility feedback connected the body first.

arbitrary.text: The required order for connecting the body before the eye muscles felt somewhat arbitrary; the result did not explain why that order was necessary.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter if it explored another connection as clearly as the contrast between light and nerve signals. I would hope for fewer repetitive fitting steps.
